source.title: Does Machine Unlearning Truly Remove Knowledge?
source.authors: Haokun Chen; Yue-Qi Zhang; Yuan-Wei Bi; Yao Zhang; Tong Liu; Jin-He Bi; Jian Lan; Jindong Gu; Claudia Großer; D. Krompass; N. Navab; Volker Tresp

page_placements.theme: Recovery by internal perturbations other than direction ablation

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates prompt-based and activation-based audits of unlearned models, using its own benchmarks and ROUGE-L rather than reproducing the specified fine-tuning, ablation, or quantization attacks.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports ROUGE-L for unlearned baselines and multiple auditors. Table 2 reports sampled-output results. The paper also gives a qualitative WHP example. ActPert is an activation-perturbation audit, not an ablation of one activation direction. Values from cited studies in Related Work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study runs prompt-based attacks on models unlearned with GA, GD, KL, RT/IDK, DPO, NPO and others: AOA role-play, ICL, MASK+ICL, GCG and SoftGCG. It measures with ROUGE-L whether answers to the targeted facts come back, on RWKU, TOFU and the original WHP checkpoint. That bears directly on version E and on A's claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge. The method and measure differ from the originals' (WMDP accuracy; Lynch et al.'s familiarity and other evaluations), so this is T2. ActPert adds a layer-wise activation difference. It is not a single-direction ablation or an analysis of blocking versus deletion, so C is not tested. B, D and F are not tested either.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that residual knowledge stays accessible to audits after unlearning, and that preference-based methods are more robust than refusal-based (RT/IDK) ones. Knowledge from pretraining (RWKU, WHP) is hard to remove, while auditing has limited effect on TOFU, where the fine-tuning data is available. They also find Phi-3 more resistant to auditing than Llama. Their 'consistent gap' across benchmarks does not hold in Table 1 for TOFU or Phi-3.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates several unlearning algorithms and builds prompt-based and activation-perturbation auditing methods; it does not reproduce the specified fine-tuning, one-direction ablation, or quantization attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with model architecture, benchmark, unlearning algorithm and dataset size, auditor, and decoding setup. The paper also reports ActPert sensitivity to layer choice and noise intensity.

fits_no_version.finding: ActPert adds noise to the target-token embeddings and injects the resulting layer-wise activation differences at inference. It raises ROUGE-L in some unlearned models, for example TOFU forget01-GA 0.503 to 0.590 and RWKU Llama-3 30-GA 0.274 to 0.538. It is sensitive to layer and noise: layer 6 gives 0.394 and noise 0.04 gives 0.302, both below base (Tables 6-7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Inference-time activation addition can expose residual target knowledge in some unlearned models; the effect depends on layer index and noise scale.

record.code_released: The paper says the framework and proposed algorithm will be open-sourced upon manuscript acceptance; no URL is stated.
record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Lock-LLM (Prevent Unauthorized Knowledge Use from LLMs)
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty estimates. It uses ROUGE-L rather than a direct accuracy measure; the authors note that TOFU auditing has limited influence and that the synthetic dataset provides direct ground-truth information. The presented evidence does not establish retained general ability or near-chance unlearned accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 contains many additional auditor-by-unlearning-method combinations, and Table 2 reports sampled-generation results across those combinations. They are omitted to prioritize contrasting conditions and directly interpretable recovery examples; the paper's aggregate text says RWKU sampled maxima often exceed 0.80, while TOFU maxima reach only around 0.60. No separately assigned Table 2 rows are included.

untested.parts: Whether targeted accuracy reaches near chance (ROUGE-L has no chance level) and whether general ability is retained. Utility is discussed only qualitatively, for GA.
Entire version; no relearning or fine-tuning attack. The ICL examples are only placed in prompts.
Entire version. ActPert adds activation differences from perturbed inputs; it does not ablate a direction or analyse blocking versus deletion.
Other languages, and a systematic paraphrase evaluation. There is only an anecdotal inverse-question example.
Entire version; no robust counter-method is proposed.

missing.what: WHP quantitative row: base 0.568 (pre-unlearning 0.973); AOA 0.779, ICL 0.770, M,I 0.688, M,I,A 0.495, GCG 0.560, SoftGCG 0.713, ActPert 0.650. The A and E labels for WHP rest on it.

RWKU Llama-3 RT conditions with strong prompt recovery: 30-RT base 0.456 to AOA 0.805 / ICL 0.804 / SoftGCG 0.664, but GCG 0.399. 20-RT 0.684 to AOA 0.806 / ICL 0.820, but GCG 0.431. Pre-unlearning 0.794. The authors say RT degrades sharply once audited.
Inverse-question rephrasing on WHP: 'Who is Albus Dumbledore' is answered although the forward headmaster query is denied. Preference methods are said to fail on inverse or paraphrased queries.

record.verdict_notes:
Repair of a quarantined verdict. The merge refused it because the record's own versions block uses V1-V6. Mapped by content, not position: V1 near-chance/attacks fail = A, V2 relearning = B, V3 direction ablation = C, V4 quantization = D, V5 prompting = E, V6 counter-method = F. Every row carrying V1/V5 or V5 now has a row_fixes item stating its declared versions. r13/r14 were already 'none'.

Kept from the earlier verdict: relation, tranche, all row states and links, and the labels. All Table 1 values were re-checked against the text. Changes:
- Dropped the Table 2 sampled-maxima item from missing, because rows_left_out declares it.
- Added the GCG numbers to the RT missing item (GCG does not recover on RT) and 20-RT to the A/E label conditions.
- Reasons now say the WHP and RT numbers come from the text.

Conventions and caveats:
- Row states describe recovery (the shallowness effect). For A, an 'observed' row therefore counts against it.
- SoftGCG is an embedding-space suffix (white-box). It is kept under E as a jailbreak.
- Phi-3 30-GA unlearned scores (0.774) exceed pre-unlearning (0.629), as do all 12 Phi-3 conditions, so r5-r8 cannot show recovery.
- The reader had taken the r1-r4 values from Phi-3 or 20-GA cells.
- No uncertainty is reported. The WHP and TOFU Q&A sets are GPT-4o-generated and small (35, 16 and 80 items).

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares unlearned and audited knowledge-retrieval scores, but does not establish that targeted accuracy is near chance or directly measure retained general ability.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is performed; ICL examples are provided in prompts, not used to train the model.
ActPert perturbs target-token embeddings and injects layer-wise activation differences; it does not ablate a single activation direction or establish that unlearning only blocks access.
The study tests role-play prefixes, in-context examples, and adversarial suffixes. It does not test prompt rephrasing alone, other languages, or the full range of jailbreaks.
The proposed ActPert method is an auditor, not a counter-method that resists the tested attacks.
